title: Registry Authority Remediation
depends_on: S210 Registry Integrity Certification (all 7 chains INTACT at S210)
S214 Registry Stress Test (5/6 duplicate ownership, active conflicts)
S216 Executive Decision (13 remediation items, items 2-4)
objective: Resolve registry authority failures identified in S214. Restore single-owner-per-entity-class model established in S208 Board F. Eliminate the gap between S210's PASS verdict and S214's CONCERN finding.

s210_to_s214_regression_timeline.finding: S210 (2026-07-27) certified 7/7 registries INTACT with 0 duplicate authority claims. S214 (same date, later) found 5/6 registries with duplicate ownership paths and active authority conflicts.
s210_to_s214_regression_timeline.root_cause: S210 verified the S208 authority model as-designed. S214 tested the model against live workspace drift. Between S210 and S214, S371, S853, S826, S829, and other waves created divergent registry artifacts that the authority model did not automatically reconcile.
s210_to_s214_regression_timeline.gap: The S208 authority model defines the CHAIN (raw > runtime > generated > reports) but has no automated enforcement of chain consistency. Registries can diverge from raw files without triggering any governance guard rule.

registry_authority_remediation.principle: PER ENTITY CLASS, EXACTLY ONE AUTHORITATIVE SOURCE. All other representations are DERIVED — never independent. Derived representations must carry a NOT_AUTHORITATIVE header. Any script that creates a new derived representation must register it with the primary registry.

derived_packages.new_requirement: Every session package must be registered in session_registry.json. Registration is MANDATORY — not optional. Add PRE-WRITE gate: script must verify registration entry exists before writing a new package.

derived_reports.new_requirement: Every session status report must reference its session_registry.json entry. Status reports are DERIVED — the registry is authoritative for session existence.

script_catalog.new_requirement: Create scripts/SCRIPT_REGISTRY.json — catalog every script with purpose, authority level, and last execution date. Scripts without registry entries are flagged as UNTRACKED.

remediation.reconciliation_rule: Every new session must write EXACTLY ONE entry to session_registry.json before any package file is written. Package file write gate checks registry entry exists.

registries.current_state: 2 competing namespaces: CH- (challenge_registry.json, 35 entries) and DL- (DEFECT_LIBRARY.md, 36 entries + 2 tracked notes). Different ID namespaces track the same entity class (content issues).
conflicts: CH- and DL- namespaces are not 1:1 mapped
Different status models: CH- uses OPEN/TRIAGED/RESOLVED; DL- uses Open/Resolved/In Progress/Superseded

remediation.recommendation: UNIFY under a single namespace. DL- (DEFECT_LIBRARY.md) is the authoritative defect catalog. CH- (challenge registry) is a user-facing intake form.

unified_model.authoritative_defect_catalog: knowledge/DEFECT_LIBRARY.md — DL- namespace. All confirmed defects live here.
unified_model.challenge_intake: scripts/output/challenge_registry.json — CH- namespace. User-raised challenges before triage.
unified_model.mapping_rule: Every CH- entry that graduates to a confirmed defect receives a DL-ID. The CH→DL mapping must be recorded in both registries. CH- entries that are dismissed (not defects) remain CH- only.
unified_model.conflict_resolution: When CH- and DL- descriptions of the same issue diverge, the DL- entry is authoritative. CH- is the unverified claim; DL- is the verified finding.

registries.current_state: SINGLE SOURCE — 5 REC-IDs. Cleanest registry. routing.json is derived, not competing.

remediation.registration_gap: Every session that produces a remediation recommendation must register a REC-ID. The 5 records represent only a fraction of actual recommendations made across 180+ sessions.
remediation.new_requirement: REC-ID creation is MANDATORY for any session that recommends a remediation action affecting ≥1 QID. The registry must grow proportionally with session count.

single_source_recertification.success_criterion: Exactly 1 authoritative source per entity class. All derived representations traceable to authorative source. Zero independent (non-derived) competing registries.

new_rule_proposal.description: Any script or agent that creates a file claiming registry-authority over an already-owned entity class is BLOCKED. All derived registries must carry NOT_AUTHORITATIVE header. Any script that writes to a derived registry without regenerating from the authoritative source is BLOCKED.
new_rule_proposal.detection: At write time: check whether target file path matches a known derived registry. If yes, verify the write is a regeneration from the authoritative source (not a hand-edit or independent write).
